persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Nancy, 64, who runs the Operation Christmas Child shoebox drive at her church in Texas. Bags of gifts are arriving, and the pastor asks you: how many complete boxes can we pack, and what do we still need?

challenge.intro: Now you are Nancy at the church in Texas. The counts are all zero. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Operation Christmas Child Assistant with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. Every count is now 0 and the goal shows 100. (Do not use '↻ start a new drive' — it keeps the goal and any items you added.)

tasks.text: Your church wants to pack 40 boxes this year. Tell the app.
tasks.hint: Look for the drive's goal near the top, under the big number.

tasks.text: Mrs Johnson brought 25 toothbrushes. Count them in.
tasks.hint: Find Toothbrushes in the list. Type the number in its small box and tap ＋, or tap its count.

tasks.text: 40 packs of crayons came in. Later you found that 4 packs were broken and threw them away. Make the count right.
tasks.hint: Crayons should end at 36. Tap its count: there is a way to take some out.

tasks.text: Your church decided every box must also have a jump rope. Jump ropes are not on the list. Add them, make them count for every box, and count in the 12 that came today.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('church_drive_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.items))return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('jump rope')||f('jumprope')||f('skipping rope');return !!i&&!!i.box&&!i.plenty&&parseFloat(i.q)===12;}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add the item at the bottom of the list, then tap its NAME — one switch says it goes in every set.

tasks.text: Someone gave so many tennis balls that you will never run out. Tell the app to stop counting them.
tasks.hint: Tap the name 'Balls/ tennis and other' and look for 'We have plenty'.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: counts the gifts that come in for a collection drive
tells you how many complete boxes you can pack, limited by the item that runs out first
shows what you still need, so you can ask people for it

lines: This short video explains the Operation Christmas Child Assistant. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, what is Operation Christmas Child? Each fall, churches fill shoeboxes with small gifts, like a toothbrush, a notebook, pencils and a toy, and the boxes go to children around the world.
Now the problem. People bring in bags of crayons, socks and toothbrushes. They pile up in the hallway, and nobody knows how many full boxes that makes, or what to buy next.
Here is the key idea. A box is only complete if it has one of every important thing. Ninety toothbrushes and four notebooks make four complete boxes, not ninety.
This app counts what comes in, and does that math for you. It works for any collection where you count things: a food drive, a school supplies drive, a coat drive.
Who uses it? Whoever is collecting: a church volunteer, a missions team, a school club, or a family.
Let us look at the screen. At the top is the big number, Complete sets, right now. This is how many full boxes you can pack today.
Below it, in red, the app tells you which item runs out first. When you reach your goal, it turns green and says so.
Next is the drive's goal: how many boxes you want to make. Tap the box and type a number.
Under the goal are the drop-off week, with the days left, and the shipping donation for your goal.
Then the long list, Everything, A to Z. Each item has a count. A gold EVERY SET tag means every box needs it, and underneath it says how many more you need.
To add things, tap the green plus for one. For a whole bag, type how many in the small how many box, then tap plus. The minus takes one away.
You can also tap the number itself. A box asks, How many came in? Type a number, or tap a quick number, then tap Add them.
If some went out to be packed, tap Took some out. If you counted again, tap Fix the total. Cancel closes it without changing anything.
Now tap the name of an item. Its own page opens. Goes in every set means every box needs it, so it counts for the big number.
We have plenty means you can stop counting it. Here you can also add or take away five or ten, type an exact count, or remove the item. Tap Done to close.
To add a new item, scroll down to the box that says add an item, type a name, and tap Add.
Back at the top, the green button, Send the group what we still need, writes a message listing everything still missing.
You can change any of the words, then tap Text it, Email it, or Copy. Nothing is sent until you tap send yourself.
The line called What is not allowed any more lists things that must not go in a box, like soap and toothpaste.
Next year, tap start a new drive at the very bottom. Counts go to zero, and your item list stays.
How to start? Set your goal, then count the first bag of donations. That is your first two minutes, and the big number starts to move.
Privacy: your counts stay on this phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you send the message yourself.
The Operation Christmas Child Assistant is nineteen dollars, once. Profits help students in Kenya stay in school.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour and help, any time you need them.
